pairs.subject: concurrent-vcs
pairs.evidence: src/lib/org/registry-view.ts:280 This context's only contact with version control is this fire-and-forget refresh, and its callee (src/lib/registry/local-registry.ts) only runs read-only `git rev-parse HEAD` / `ls-tree HEAD` on the paired registry checkout. Nothing in the context stages, commits, stashes, rebases or creates worktrees, so the subject's precondition (sessions editing and committing in a shared checkout) does not hold here. A ripgrep of src/lib/org and src/features/shared/registry found no read-tree, git stash or GIT_INDEX_FILE.

pairs.subject: concurrent-vcs
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts:5 The concurrency this context handles is webhook redelivery, made idempotent on the Polar order id; it performs no VCS operation at all. A ripgrep of src/app/api/billing, src/app/api/org/plan, src/app/pricing, src/features/admin/settings and src/lib found no read-tree, git stash or update-index, so the shared-checkout commit techniques have no surface here.

pairs.subject: concurrent-vcs
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/org/import/route.ts:33 The "claim" in this context is a database ScanJob row that dedups concurrent scans of one repo, not a session's claim on paths in a shared git checkout. The routes scan via the GitHub API and persist to the DB; they never stage, commit, stash or create worktrees. A ripgrep of the import/repos/scan/watch/schedule/active/cron-rescan route dirs and src/lib/db found no read-tree, git stash or GIT_INDEX_FILE.
